nodes.label: Security Review Against the §12 Checklist
nodes.rationale: Every item in the security specification's checklist with its status and where it is enforced. Nothing is marked confirmed on the strength of code alone: where a test proves it the test is named, and where the proof is a database privilege the privilege was exercised against a real database.

nodes.label: Checklist Status Summary
nodes.rationale: 23 confirmed, 3 partial, 4 deferred of 30. Deferred items are listed with the same prominence as confirmed ones because a review that buries them is worth nothing. None are oversights: each is an integration no reference document specifies, or deployment-shaped work Stage 21 settles.

nodes.label: MFA on Dashboard Accounts — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: The challenge is signed for a separate JWT audience so the existing audience check rejects it anywhere an access token is expected — separation enforced by a control that already existed rather than a new rule someone has to remember. A TOTP code cannot be replayed, verification is rate-limited per account rather than per IP, and the account is re-read at every step so instant revocation holds inside the window between password and second factor.

nodes.label: STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED Caveat on the MFA Claim
nodes.rationale: Named here rather than only in the decision log, because the heading claims enforcement on every dashboard account and that claim now carries a condition. What makes it acceptable is that it cannot be turned in the place where turning it matters — loadEnv throws in production, the handler re-checks at the branch, a typo fails closed, and the resulting sign-in audits distinctly.

nodes.label: No MFA Reset Path and No Step-Up Re-Authentication
nodes.rationale: An account that loses both its authenticator and its recovery codes is locked out permanently. A reset is itself security-sensitive — whoever can reset MFA can take over an administrator account — so it needs dual control or an out-of-band identity check rather than a convenient endpoint. Export and benefit editing sit behind permissions and the audit log but not behind a fresh second factor.

nodes.label: Scope-Spread Clobbering Defect
nodes.rationale: A real defect in the security document's own illustrative snippet. Every lookup returned the caller's own record instead of 404 — a 200 where the answer had to be 404, failing open while looking correct. Fixed with AND composition and pinned by a regression test that demonstrates the old behaviour explicitly.

nodes.label: Missing Verification Session Defect
nodes.rationale: Surfaced by the fetch-then-check guard during Stage 7: the redemption endpoint accepted any member id an outlet account sent, whether or not they had ever resolved that member. Now an HMAC over (staffUserId, memberId, issuedAt) issued by resolve and required by record, tested for expiry, wrong member, wrong account and forged signature.

nodes.label: Database-Level Redemption Immutability — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: Exercised against a real database: the application connects as pgp_app, which holds only SELECT and INSERT on Redemption. Migrations run as the schema owner through Prisma's directUrl, because an owner cannot be denied its own tables and the revocation would otherwise be theatre.

nodes.label: Idempotency Key Lookup Scoped to the Caller's Outlet
nodes.rationale: The key is client-supplied, so an unscoped lookup would let a guessed key disclose another outlet's redemption — member id, benefit, party size, bill amount. The same key with different content returns 409 rather than silently returning the original, because that would hide a client bug.

nodes.label: Small-Cohort Suppression — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: The cohort is distinct members, not rows: four redemptions by one member is a cohort of one, and it is the member the report must not identify. The cohort size is withheld along with the figures, since '3 members' is the same disclosure stated outright.

nodes.label: Log Redaction — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: Two mechanisms because either alone leaves a gap: pino redact paths for shapes the app logs itself, and a serializer that walks whatever a caller passes at any depth. The second is what makes log.info({ member }) safe — the call nobody anticipates, made while debugging something else. Opaque references pass through, or redaction would strip the identifiers that make an entry useful.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Log — Confirmed
nodes.rationale: UPDATE and DELETE on AuditLog are revoked from the application role, so a caller cannot rewrite its own trail. Entries carry the membership number, never the name, and a failed login does not record the attempted email — that would write attacker-chosen strings, and occasionally a real address typed into the wrong box, into the trail.

nodes.label: Deferred — Pepper and Signing Keys in a KMS
nodes.rationale: No KMS exists in this build's stack or in any reference document. PASSWORD_PEPPER is an environment variable — at least not colocated with the hashes it protects, which is the property the pepper exists for, but not the mechanism required. The same applies to the verification-session HMAC secret and the JWT signing key, and to key rotation with a kid so old tokens verify during rollover.

nodes.label: Deferred — Real-Time Alerting
nodes.rationale: Every alertable event — repeated failed lookups, refresh-token reuse, bulk export, out-of-hours access, excess lookup volume, denial spikes — is recorded with a distinct audit action, so the data exists. Nothing consumes it, and no alerting destination is named in any reference document. This is what makes the audit log forensic rather than preventive.

nodes.label: Deferred — Security Headers and CORS Allowlist
nodes.rationale: The item most likely to be forgotten, because everything works without it right up until it is deployed. In development the clients reach the API through a Vite proxy, so requests are same-origin and no CORS policy is exercised — the gap is invisible locally and appears immediately on first deployment. CORS_ORIGIN_* variables are named in .env.example but unread.

nodes.label: Deferred — httpOnly Cookies and CSRF
nodes.rationale: Mitigated at review time by no client storing a token in localStorage or sessionStorage — all held it in a module-scoped variable, unreadable by an injected script and gone when the tab closes, at the cost of a sign-in on every reload. Residual risk: bearer tokens in JavaScript memory remain reachable by XSS in the same context. Later addressed by the httpOnly refresh cookie decision.

nodes.label: Deferred — Data Protection Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Explicitly not an engineering task. Failing to carry one out carries an administrative fine of up to QAR 1,000,000 on its own, independent of any breach, and the hosting region must be settled before infrastructure is built given restrictions on transferring personal data outside Qatar. Blocking for launch rather than for development.

nodes.label: Partial Items: Anonymisation, Special-Category Data, Pagination Caps
nodes.rationale: No anonymisation endpoint exists and no stage lists one. No special-category data is satisfied by construction — Redemption has no treatment column — but marked partial because the guard is the schema as it stands, not a test. The export cap of 5000 rows is high enough that the full membership is effectively reachable, so the cap is not doing protective work there.

nodes.label: Per-Device Outlet Authentication Addendum
nodes.rationale: The current authority wherever older verification-page or Google-default text conflicts. An outlet holds exactly outlet:queue, outlet:fulfil and outlet:resolve and notably not redemptions:record, because that route takes the outlet from the request body — holding it would be a way to record against another outlet's room. The exchange endpoint hashes malformed and truncated values through the same indexed lookup and uniform 401 path as unknown credentials.

nodes.label: Google Sheets Mirror as a Conditional External Surface
nodes.rationale: Code controls confirmed; production activation not yet approved. Enabling it creates a standing bulk export outside Fastify RBAC, so the hotel must first approve Workspace and its data residency, disable link sharing, restrict named humans to Viewer, grant Editor only to the service identity, and store and rotate its key through the deployment secret manager.

nodes.label: What I Would Fix First
nodes.rationale: In order: MFA on dashboard accounts, security headers and a CORS allowlist, httpOnly cookies with CSRF, alerting, then a KMS retiring three environment-variable secrets. Items 2 and 3 are ordinary deployment work; item 1 was a conflict between the build plan and the security specification needing a human to resolve it.
